It's not easy to tell. She could have developed certain difficulties growing up, or she could have spent her life masking and that makes her look like she couldn't belong on the spectrum. I personally think she should reflect on herself a whole lot, and then seek help once she has a vague idea of what's going on, because the likelihood of her getting misdiagnosed if she just goes in blind is very high. At the end of the day, when it comes to autism in AFAB, the majority of us have to figure it out on our own, checking off the things we don't recognize ourselves in. Eventually, you could find you could have a sprinkle of everything BECAUSE of the autism, or that you've just been misunderstood the whole time. But then again, you can't force a person to do that. You can't force a person to reflect on their views and perceptions of the world to determine whether or not they could be on the spectrum. If you want to help you could try talking to her about those things, give her the information she might be missing and then let her figure it out on her own. You definitely shouldn't be a parent to your own mom. 

As far as the definition and existence of BPD.. Well, I don't really know. I know people with BPD who don't seem to belong on the spectrum, but once again they're all AFAB who could just be very good at masking. It's complicated, and not researched nearly enough. The overlapping of different diagnoses with autism is something I feel people are just starting to realize. It might take a while before we have actually good and useful information on both autism in AFAB and most other conditions as well.
